title: Model serving SLO lifecycle playbook and tactical backlog
content:
Purpose:
This working playbook captures a practical, sprint-oriented approach to design, roll out, and operate SLOs for model-serving endpoints (hosted + dedicated + private). Target audience: SREs, serving runtime engineers, platform, product owners, observability, and solutions engineers.

Scope and assumptions:
- Focus: production inference endpoints (text generation/chat/embeddings) exposed by Redwood API and Dedicated clusters.
- Out of scope: offline model training jobs and developer preview endpoints.
- Assume telemetry pipelines exist (token-level traces, request metadata, per-route tags) but may need new SLIs.

Key definitions for this playbook:
- SLI: measurable signal (success_rate, p99_latency, model_quality_regressions).
- SLO: target bound on an SLI (e.g., success_rate >= 99.95% over 30d).
- Error budget: allowable unit of failure tied to SLO.
- Canary: a small traffic slice used to validate a change.

High-level phases (90-day lens):
1) Discover (weeks 1–2): inventory endpoints, define stakeholders per route, capture current SLI baselines. Output: route inventory CSV and baseline report.
2) Design (weeks 3–4): pick SLI candidates for each route (latency, success, token-dropouts, model-quality), propose SLO thresholds and burn policies. Output: per-route SLO draft + runbook template.
3) Pilot (weeks 5–9): instrument missing telemetry, run canary SLOs for 2–3 representative routes (one low-latency, one high-throughput, one private deployment). Output: pilot retro + adjustments.
4) Rollout (weeks 10–13): tiered rollout to remaining routes with automation for alert creation and error-budget gating. Output: rollout audit log + SLO configs in the repo.
5) Operate (ongoing): monitor burn, automate rollback and capacity scaling triggers, quarterly SLO reviews.

90-day tactical backlog (by sprint):
Sprint A (Discovery, 2 weeks):
- Task: Extract route inventory from API gateway and console (owner: Platform).
- Task: Lightweight baseline job (load: 3 days) to compute p50/p95/p99 and error rates (owner: Observability).
- Task: Stakeholder map (owner: Product + Solutions Eng).

Sprint B (Design, 2 weeks):
- Task: Define canonical SLI set: request_success_rate (2xx), p99_server_latency, kv-cache-hit-rate, model-quality-check (A/B prompt test). (owner: SRE + Applied ML)
- Task: Proposed SLOs: example targets: 99.95% 30d success for hosted, 99.9% for private; p99 latency target depends on route profile (documented ranges). (owner: SRE)
- Task: Draft runbook template (severity, initial mitigation steps, error-budget action). (owner: SRE)

Sprint C (Pilot, 5 weeks):
- Task: Add missing spans and labels to traces (owner: Serving runtime).
- Task: Extend metrics exporter with per-route tags, token breakdown (owner: Observability).
- Task: Build canary automation: traffic splitter, profiling capture, automatic SLO evaluation script. (owner: Platform + Release Eng)
- Task: Run load-injection tests against canary routes and measure burn. (owner: SRE + Performance Eng)
- Task: Run small model quality evals for canary (owner: Applied ML)

Sprint D (Rollout + Automation, 4 weeks):
- Task: Convert pilot configs into templated SLO manifests and commit to telemetry-configs repo. (owner: Observability)
- Task: Create alert rules: threshold + rate-of-change + error-budget-exhaustion alarms; wire into oncall rota (owner: SRE).
- Task: Add automated remediation playbooks: scaled fallback routing to lower-cost model variants and capacity burst triggers (owner: Platform + Serving runtime).
- Task: Training session for oncall teams on new runbooks (owner: SRE + DevEx).

Owners & RACI (simple):
- SRE (A): SLO policy, runbook, alerting, oncall playbooks.
- Serving runtime (R): instrumentation touches, throttle/fallback hooks.
- Observability (R): telemetry plumbing, dashboards, SLO evaluation jobs.
- Platform/Release Eng (C): canary plumbing, rollout automation.
- Product/Applied ML (C): define model-quality SLI, validate quality checks.
- Solutions Eng (C): customer-specific constraints for private deployments.

Suggested canonical SLI definitions (concrete):
- request_success_rate: fraction of requests returning 2xx within 60s window. Aggregation: per-route, per-customer where applicable.
- p99_server_latency_ms: 99th percentile server-side tail latency excluding network egress. Window: 1h & 30d.
- token_generation_rate_ok: fraction of tokens produced without internal retry or truncation.
- model_regression_score: pass_rate on a curated prompt set (daily).

Example SLO candidates (illustrative):
- Hosted-chat: success_rate >= 99.95% (30d), p99_latency <= 350ms (30d).
- Dedicated-batch-embeddings: success_rate >= 99.9% (30d), p99_latency <= 1200ms (30d).
- Private-onprem: success_rate >= 99.9% (30d), p99_latency <= customer-agreed SLA.

Instrumentation checklist before pilot:
- Ensure every route emits route_name, model_variant, deployment_mode, customer_tier as tags.
- Token-level counters: tokens_requested, tokens_served, tokens_cached.
- Error taxonomy labels: transient, config, resource, model_failure.
- End-to-end synthetic probes for critical routes (canary probes).

Alerting & escalation pattern:
- Level 1 (warning): 5m elevated p99 or small uptick in error rate — notify oncall, auto open investigation ticket.
- Level 2 (action): error budget burn > 25% within 24h — trigger mitigation automation and paging.
- Level 3 (severe): burn > 50% or outage impact — full incident bridge and product comms.

Gating criteria for SLO promotion from pilot -> production:
- Observability: SLO exporter has <5% measurement gaps over a 7-day window.
- Stability: pilot route error budget burn <= 10% during load tests.
- Quality: no model_regression_score drop >1% on pilot set.
- Runbook: playbook validated and rehearsed by oncall team.

Operational automations to implement during rollout:
- Auto-rollbacks for model variant changes if model_regression_score drops by threshold.
- Traffic-steering: automated policy to degrade to cheaper variant under sustained burn.
- Error budget-aware throttles: dynamically lower concurrency for non-critical traffic tiers.

Metrics and dashboards to create (minimum):
- Per-route SLO panel (current SLO vs target, 30d view).
- Error-budget burn timeline with recent incidents overlay.
- Canary comparison view (pilot vs control).
- Capacity & queueing heatmap with inference GPU utilization.

Common risks and mitigations:
- Risk: telemetry gaps for legacy routes. Mitigation: short-term synthetic probes and staged instrumentation.
- Risk: SLOs too aggressive causing frequent paging. Mitigation: use staged SLOs + error-budget smoothing policy.
- Risk: model-quality metric noisy. Mitigation: increase evaluation sample size and signal smoothing; include human-in-the-loop review for first 2 sprints.

Success criteria (end of 90 days):
- 80% of production routes have SLO manifests checked into repo and displayed in console.
- Two pilot routes operating under SLOs with documented runbooks and <10% error-budget burn during testing.
- Oncall teams trained and first live drill executed.

Open questions / decisions required:
- Agree on default SLO tiers for hosted vs dedicated vs private (product + biz input needed).
- Decide retention and granularity for per-customer SLO evaluation (privacy/cost tradeoff).
- Finalize model-quality drift threshold that triggers auto-rollback.

Next steps (immediate):
- Platform to export route inventory by EOD Friday (owner: Platform).
- Observability to share baseline report draft within 4 business days (owner: Observability).
- Schedule 90-minute cross-team kickoff to align KPI definitions (owner: SRE).

Notes to reviewers (informal):
- This doc is intentionally tactical and sprint-driven — expect edits to backlog items after kickoff.
- If your team maintains a route not listed in the inventory, flag it in the kickoff thread.
- Where possible, prefer telemetry tags over ad-hoc dashboards; we'll standardize slowly so teams can opt-in.

Appendix: quick runbook template (copied into repo after review)
- Title: <route name> SLO runbook
- SLOs: <slos>
- Symptoms: <how it looks in telemetry>
- Immediate mitigations: <circuit breakers, fallback routing, restart steps>
- Escalation: <oncall steps, pager contacts>
- Post-incident: <investigation checklist, owners, remediation timeline>

End of document.
